text:
anya: FYI onboarding "halcyon-liteq-ptq" produced repeatable malformed JSON in the funcall eval set. low-level token splits are corrupting trailing separators. :frowning:

miguel: examples? is it parse errors or schema mismatches?

anya: parse errors. They mostly show up when responses exceed ~480 tokens. acceptance dropped to ~86%.

anya: sample output (truncated):
```json
{"items": [
  {"id": 42, "op": "upsert", "data": {"k": "v"},},
  {"id": 43, "op": "delete", "data": {}}
}
```

olivia: trailing comma inside object and extra closing brace. smells like token boundary insertion or a suffix token that used to be part of a multi-byte token is now split.

raj: did you run single-request vs batched inference? kv-cache batching is our usual suspect.

anya: yes. single-request + temp=0.0 improved acceptance to 97% (latency +7%). batched (prod) stayed ~85%

sam: interim mitigation: add a lightweight sanitizer that runs a tolerant repair pass: remove trailing commas, balance brackets, then run strict schema validator. repaired ~65% of failures.

miguel: for the remaining hard failures, what about a 1-2 token suffix regen? i.e. re-query the model with the last N tokens and an instruction: "COMPLETE_JSON_ONLY". keep regen opt-in.

olivia: note that regen can change semantics; acceptable only if callers opt into "schema-first" mode. need an API flag and audit log.

anya: implemented a PoC for regen opt-in and a sanitizer. PoC script here (local):
```bash
python tools/json_repair.py --in sample_resp.json --out fixed.json --regen-if-unfixable
```

sam: can you open a canary matrix? grid: single vs batch x temp [0.0,0.1,0.2] x regen opt-in on/off.

ci-bot: Pipeline created: ml/halcyon-liteq/ptq-schema-matrix. runs: batch,single x temps 0.0,0.1,0.2 x regen:false,true. ETA ~6h

raj: longer-term fixes: two angles
- tokenization alignment test for quant on onboarding harness (pre/post token sequences)
- runtime prefix-padding to avoid splitting critical punctuation tokens across batch boundaries

miguel: + add metric to Console: model.version.schema_hard_fail_rate and split by deployment_mode (hosted/dedicated/private) and by batching (single/batch).

anya: filing JIRA tasks: ML-940 (onboard corpus + token-diff), ML-941 (repair + regen opt-in), INF-873 (runtime padding experiment). Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
